intent: Suggest order quantities for each product for the upcoming Brunch weekend to meet expected sales without overstocking, subject to human review and approval.

definitions.name: Expected sales
definitions.text: Start from each product's average over the last four weekends. Products on offer sell about 40% more, the kit's ingredients about 10% more, and everything else about 15% more. Add 40 units for ingredients used in the kit (a sourdough loaf, a pack of avocados, and a pack of feta). Round up to whole units.

groups.quote: eggs, cherry tomatoes and rocket are on offer
a sourdough loaf, a pack of ripe avocados and a pack of feta

definitions.formula: ceil((double(record.weekend_1 + record.weekend_2 + record.weekend_3 + record.weekend_4) / double(constants.four_weekends)) * (1.0 + double(key in groups.on_offer ? constants.offer_boost_pct : (key in groups.kit_ingredients ? constants.kit_ingredient_boost_pct : constants.other_boost_pct)) / 100.0) + double(key in groups.kit_ingredients ? constants.kit_extra_units : 0))

examples.why: Average over 4 weekends is (28 + 31 + 30 + 31) / 4 = 30. SD-01 is a kit ingredient, so it sells 10% more: 30 * 1.10 = 33. Plus 40 extra units for the kit: 33 + 40 = 73. Ceil is 73.
Average over 4 weekends is (19 + 21 + 20 + 20) / 4 = 20. EG-06 is on offer, so it sells 40% more: 20 * 1.40 = 28. Ceil is 28.
Average over 4 weekends is (9 + 11 + 10 + 10) / 4 = 10. LM-04 is neither on offer nor a kit ingredient, so it sells 15% more: 10 * 1.15 = 11.5. Ceil is 12.

definitions.name: Target stock level
definitions.text: Enough stock to cover expected sales plus the category's safety margin.

examples.why: Expected sales is 73. Bakery safety pct is 10%. 73 * (1 + 10 / 100) = 80.3
Expected sales is 4. Ambient safety pct is 5%. 4 * (1 + 5 / 100) = 4.2

definitions.name: Ripe avocados limit
definitions.text: Ripe avocados don't keep, so do not order more than we will sell.

examples.why: AV-RR expected sales is 65, net stock is 12, order 10 + 12 = 22 <= 65.
AV-RR expected sales is 65, net stock is 12, order 60 + 12 = 72 > 65.
The proposed order of 16 loaves is exactly 2 cases of 8 loaves, so it is in whole cases.
The proposed order of 15 loaves is not a multiple of the case size of 8 loaves (15 leaves a remainder of 7).
The proposed order of 20 packs is exactly 2 cases of 10 packs, so it is in whole cases.
The proposed order of 25 packs is not a multiple of the case size of 10 packs (25 leaves a remainder of 5).

definitions.name: Supplier delivery limit
definitions.text: Never order more than the supplier can deliver.

examples.why: The proposed order of 72 sourdough loaves does not exceed the supplier maximum order limit of 72 units.
The proposed order of 80 sourdough loaves exceeds the supplier maximum order limit of 72 units.
The produce wholesaler has no maximum order limit for ripe avocados, so any order is within the supplier limit.

definitions.name: Arrival before opening
definitions.text: Only order what arrives before Saturday's opening.
definitions.formula: order == 0 || record.delivery_day < constants.saturday || (record.delivery_day == constants.saturday && record.delivery_time < constants.opening_time)

examples.why: Local bakery delivers on Saturday at 06:00 (360 minutes), which is before Saturday 07:00 (420 minutes), so ordering 40 units is allowed.
An order of 0 units is always allowed regardless of delivery time.
Produce wholesaler delivers on Friday (day 5), which is before Saturday, so ordering 20 units is allowed.

definitions.name: Cover target stock level
definitions.text: Aim for enough stock to cover expected sales plus the category's safety margin. If that isn't possible, flag it for a person to decide.

examples.why: On hand 0, reserved 0, inbound 0 plus proposed order of 88 equals 88, which is at least the target stock level of 80.3.
On hand 0, reserved 0, inbound 0 plus proposed order of 72 equals 72, which is less than the target stock level of 80.3.
